editorial:
Imagine you are stuck on a lonely Scottish island in the 1940s with a group of strict nuns. A huge storm is hitting, and suddenly, a mysterious baby shows up in a basket on the doorstep. While most of the nuns want to help, Sister Agnes is convinced the baby is actually the Devil in disguise. She tries to kill the child, which gets her locked away, but that is only where the real scary stuff begins. You will feel the tension grow as the wind howls outside and the nuns start to lose their grip on what is real and what is a trick of the mind. Sister Eleanor has to step up to save everyone while the convent turns into a nightmare.

The acting is top-notch, and the way the movie builds up the fear without relying on cheap jumpscares is great. Some parts move a bit slow at first, but the second half is a wild ride that keeps you guessing. If you love spooky stories about religion and isolated places, you need to see this.
endingExplained: At the end, it turns out the baby really was an evil entity used to test the nuns. Sister Agnes was right about the child, but her madness made everyone ignore her. In the final scenes, the baby transforms into a demon that kills most of the sisters. Sister Eleanor manages to survive by showing true faith and using a holy relic to banish the creature back to hell just as the storm clears.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gothic horror and creepy convents.
